Assumptions:
All countries want to maximise
wellbeing
Injections:
View hardship as a good thing, making us
more resilient

Assumptions:
Current levels of alcohol-related harm
are too high, impacting negatively on
our wellbeing, and on our reputation as
a healthy society
Injections:
Use better ways of repairing the harm.
Avoid negative publicity; get drunks off
streets

Assumptions:
Supermarkets are biggest culprits
making cheap alcohol readily available
Injections:
Introduce other measures to restrict or
reduce sales in supermarkets; focus on
reducing binge drinking directly

Assumptions:
NZers want the convenience of having
supermarkets, but supermarkets will
close if they don’t make enough profit
Injections:
Supermarkets could afford to reduce
their profits and still survive

Assumptions:
Alcohol is the only reason supermarkets
make a profit
Injections:
There are plenty of other products
supermarkets could make a profit from.
Reduce costs instead, like advertising
budgets.
Subsidise supermarkets from the
government health budget if a ban goes
through

Assumptions:
A ban is a complete ban on sales by
supermarkets at all times
Injections:
Mid-way options exist, such as:
1. Ban alcohol sales during certain hours, or
in certain areas, or restrict the location,
visibility within the supermarket,‘a store
within a store’with tight controls.
2. Ban alcohol sales in supermarkets but
allow them to set up a separate liquor store
nearby.
3. Ban supermarket sales only near areas
where problem drinking occurs
